# `prompt_length_to_header`

Estimates prompt length and promotes a route key when a model limit is exceeded.

## Configuration Notes

The estimate is deliberately provider-neutral and conservative. It counts text in common prompt-bearing fields (`messages`, `prompt`, `input`, `system`, and `instructions`). ASCII text is rounded up at three characters per token; non-ASCII text is charged at one token per UTF-8 byte so emoji and CJK input cannot be silently underestimated. It is a routing heuristic, not a billing or quota token count.

The filter removes any client-supplied copy of its output header before it publishes a derived value. A following core `router` can exact-match the configured `overflow` key and select a larger-context cluster.

## Configuration

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `routes` | object[] | yes | Per-model input limits and overflow route keys. |
| `routes[].model` | string | yes | Exact request-body model name. |
| `routes[].max_input_tokens` | integer | yes | Largest estimated input-token count that remains on the default route. |
| `routes[].overflow` | string | yes | Bounded value promoted when the estimate exceeds `max_input_tokens`. |
| `header` | string | no | Header that receives an overflow route key. Defaults to `X-Prompt-Route`. |
| `max_body_bytes` | integer | no | Maximum JSON request body buffered for estimation. |

## Example

```yaml
filter: prompt_length_to_header
header: X-Prompt-Route
routes:
  - model: small-context-model
    max_input_tokens: 8192
    overflow: large-context
```
